correctness.rationale: The five-point DFT gives squared norms (2/5)|S_1|^2 and S_0^2/5+(2/5)|S_2|^2 for the two projections, with S_r=sum_j n_j zeta^(rj). For S_0=0, the coefficient polynomial is divisible over Z by 1-z, and its value at zeta is nonzero for nonzero n because the only degree-at-most-four polynomial relation is a multiple of Phi_5 with nonzero augmentation. The two complex embeddings and their conjugates give |S_1|^2|S_2|^2=5|N(beta_n)|, proving the stated product and unit equality condition, and excluding a nonzero integer point of E. For a nearest vector n to f with distance delta, nonzero augmentation gives delta>=1/sqrt(5); n=0 gives delta=||f||. Otherwise orthogonal projection gives (||f||+delta)delta>=2/sqrt(5). Along any unbounded sequence with bounded ||f|| delta, delta tends to zero, proving the lower liminf bound. The two absolute embeddings of 1+zeta+zeta^(-1) are phi and 1/phi. The augmentation-zero coefficient vectors of (1-zeta) times its k-th power give increasing projected lengths r_k and complementary lengths exactly 2/(sqrt(5)r_k). Taking f_k to be the projected vector gives the matching upper liminf. The three nearest-vector cases give amplification at most sqrt(5)B, 1, or (sqrt(5)/2)B(B+sqrt(5)/2), all at most 2B^2 for B>=2. Since r_0<2 and r_(k+1)=phi r_k, the largest r_k<=B strictly exceeds B/phi, proving the stated strict lower bound. The scripts were inspected, not run; exact determinant tests and floating comparisons are supplementary.
residual_risks: The radius B in L(B) bounds the input difference from zero as defined, not independently the radii of two endpoints; two endpoints of norm at most B can have difference norm up to 2B.
The finitary bounds show the sharp exponent, not an exact leading constant for L(B) or a noisy estimator guarantee.

originality.rationale: Best-of-knowledge pass for the sharp folded-distance liminf and explicit radius-dependent inverse growth for this signal plane in its specified Euclidean normalization. Qualitative injectivity is already covered. The product identity and its unit equality mechanism are a direct cyclotomic embedding-norm specialization, not a new ideal-lattice theorem. The distinct claim transfers this product to the actual nearest point of the full integer lattice for arbitrary real signals and pairs that lower bound with a unit sequence and a finite radius cutoff.

value.rationale: Global injectivity of this natural smallest prime-length nontrivial real first-harmonic model does not reveal the severity of near collisions. The sharp liminf and uniform quadratic growth bounds quantify how conditioning deteriorates with energy, distinguishing the inverse problem from a simple uniqueness check. The exact product makes the near collisions explicit without claiming that standard norm theory is new or that arbitrary sampling has this rate.
